entries.description: This dataset is made available for research purposes only
entries.subject: This dataset
entries.object: made available for research purposes only

spans.text: **The dataset's own site states a research-only restriction with no named open license.** slanglab.cs.umass.edu/TwitterAAE (fetched and read directly, 2026-08-19) says, verbatim, twice, once for each corpus it hosts: *"This dataset is made available for research purposes only."* No CC license, no public-domain statement, no redistribution grant of any kind accompanies that sentence.

(The GitHub repository `github.com/slanglab/twitteraae` carries an MIT license, but that MIT grant covers the *code* — the demographic classifier model and its Python implementation — not the tweet *data*, which is hosted separately as a zip on the lab's own site and is never mentioned in the repository's license file.)

entries.subject: paper's own

spans.text: **The paper's own release plan was IDs-only, and current platform ToS is tighter than it was in 2016.** The source paper (Blodgett, Green, and O'Connor, EMNLP 2016, "Demographic Dialectal Variation in Social Media: A Case Study of African-American English," read in full from the ACL Anthology PDF) says exactly this about its own two derived corpora: *"Our two resulting user corpora contain 830,000 and 7.3 million tweets, for which we are making their message IDs available for further research (in conformance with the Twitter API's Terms of Service)."* That is the authors' own stated distribution plan in the paper that introduced this dataset: message IDs, not raw text, specifically because of Twitter's ToS — in 2016.
